references.text: Jesus confirms that he does not speak on his own authority, but that the Father has given him a command to speak, just as in John 11:42 where he says that the Father always hears him and that he speaks because of the crowd.
Jesus explains that the Son can do nothing by himself, but only what he sees the Father doing, which underscores the same complete obedience and dependence expressed in John 11:42.
Jesus says that he always does what is pleasing to the Father and that the Father is with him, a direct parallel to the claim in John 11:42 that the Father always hears him.
David expresses confidence that God hears him, a theme which Jesus confirms as a constant reality in his relationship with the Father in John 11:42.
